Subject: ACME - request for exec review: regional competitive safeguard & MFN ask

Team,

Quick summary: Acme (large retail customer) has pushed for three non-standard asks as part of a commitment to a 3-year reserved capacity deal worth $1.9M ARR: 1) a 35% list discount, 2) an 18-month regional exclusivity clause (North American retail, initially focused on US Southwest/West), and 3) an MFN clause that would require us to match any lower published price for comparable commitment/term. They also want a benchmark clause tying uptime/latency SLAs to financial credits if we miss targets (they propose 95th pctl latency <250ms).

Attachments: Acme_MSA_redline.pdf (their redlines), benchmark-metrics.xlsx (their proposed measurements).

Ask: I need executive guidance on whether any of these are deal-killers or if there are acceptable guardrails we can offer. Specific questions:
- Approve/deny exclusivity? If approved, suggested duration?
- MFN: allow only for published list/discounts or require parity even for private bespoke deals?
- Benchmark clause: accept credit structure or require narrower performance windows and carveouts for degradation due to customer integrations?

Business context: Acme is strategic — national footprint, potential reference, and marketplace channel opportunity. If we push too hard we risk losing the pilot, but concessions here could set a precedent.

Proposed quick counter (what sales prefers): 25% max discount if MFN removed; change exclusivity to a 12-month "preferred partner" commitment limited to specified SKU/region and with a carveout for existing contracts; tighten benchmark triggers to production-impact incidents rather than raw latency percentiles.

Please reply with framing to share back with Acme. If you want exec to decide, I'll escalate to Monica for signoff.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Steph — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers and recommended redlines: 

1) Exclusivity: we should push back. Full exclusivity for 18 months is very high risk. If this is only a marketing/preferred partner ask tied to co-marketing and referral commitments, we can consider a 12-month limited term and restrict to a narrowly defined set of products and geos (list them). We must add an explicit carveout for existing customers and resellers.

2) MFN: categorical NO to an open-ended MFN that covers private deals. If we must concede anything, limit MFN to "published list price" or "public discounts available on our website or in marketplace listings" and require parity only for the same term and committed capacity. Also add a mutuality clause (we would expect the same).

3) Benchmark clause: avoid percentile-only clauses that are easy to game. Define SLA in observable, operational terms (error-rate, tail latency under specified synthetic load), limit credits to a sliding scale with a cap, and include standard force majeure/maintenance carveouts. Any credit structure should require a dispute resolution process and a 30-day cure period.

I think we can sign off on a 25% discounted commitment if MFN is removed and exclusivity is narrowed to 12 months with carveouts. Leave legal to propose the exact redlines.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations

Appreciate the analysis. Adding commercial context: Acme is offering an accelerated commit (upfront payment for year 1 + reserved capacity) and is willing to be a marquee retail reference in exchange for stronger protections. If we refuse the exclusivity + MFN we risk losing them to competitors who will offer pockets of exclusivity.

I'm comfortable recommending a compromise to execs: 25% discount + 12-month regional "preferred partner" term (not absolute exclusivity) and a narrowly scoped MFN that only covers published discounts for comparable committed capacity/term. If execs will not approve MFN in any form, ask for approval to remove MFN and offer a 30% discount instead.

If legal can deliver the redline by EOD today we can keep momentum. Please escalate to Monica for decision if you agree.

Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts

Monica — forwarding the thread and attachments. TL;DR: Acme wants 35% discount + 18-month regional exclusivity + MFN (open-ended). Sales recommends a compromise: 25% + 12-month preferred partner wording + MFN limited to published discounts only. Rishi/legal recommend removing MFN entirely or narrowing it to published list/marketplace parity.

Why it needs exec: the MFN + exclusivity combination materially increases go-forward risk and sets precedent for other large retail deals. We need an explicit exec call on acceptable tradeoffs (discount vs MFN vs exclusivity duration).

Options for exec:
- Approve 25% discount + 12-month preferred partner clause + MFN limited to published list price for equal term/commit.
- Deny MFN entirely and approve up to 30% discount + marketing commitments.
- Deny exclusivity, allow a co-marketing "preferred partner" clause only.

Attachments included for context. Happy to jump on a quick sync if you prefer.

Best,
Stephanie

Team — thanks for the context and recommendations. After weighing risk vs. commercial value I approve the following tradeoffs for DEAL-2026-094-Acme: 

1) Discount: Approve a maximum 25% off list for the committed reserved capacity structure. No higher discount without CFO sign-off.

2) Exclusivity: DENY absolute exclusivity. Approve a 12-month "preferred partner" clause limited to specified product families and geographic clusters (West + Southwest US) with explicit carveouts for customers under existing contracts and for channel/reseller-sourced accounts. Clause must be non-blocking (Acme cannot prevent Redwood from selling to other customers).

3) MFN: DENY open-ended MFN. If Acme requires parity language we will agree only to an MFN limited to published, documented discounts (website, marketplace listings, or publicly-filed RFP pricing) for identical term and committed capacity. No parity against unpublished bespoke discounts. Include mutuality language.

4) Benchmark/SLA: Approve a performance review and a limited credit-style SLA but require narrower trigger definitions, a 30-day cure period, and a 6-month performance review that can terminate the preferred partner language if we miss sustained targets. Legal to draft capped credits (not to exceed X% of monthly fees) and dispute resolution steps.

Next steps: Legal (Laura) to produce a redline incorporating these guardrails and the exec approval note attached (exec-approval-note.pdf). Deal Desk: finalize pricing sheet and HubSpot notes; ops to prepare 6-month performance review playbook. Sales: communicate the tradeoffs to Acme and get verbal confirmation before redline exchange.

Monica Patel
VP, Commercial Strategy & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
